headline: High risk of prompt injection and data leakage via shared server datastore and file surfaces; capability conflict is also material.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write server filesystem and uses shared state via server datastore; Rasa ingests messages from external channels. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content from Rasa can be written into Flowise inputs or files and later treated as instructions. The interaction is inferred from profiles, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes upward from low.
conditions: IF Rasa message content is forwarded into Flowise files or datastore entries without sanitization
IF Flowise flows parse stored text as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Add a strict content separator between chat text and instructions
Disable any flow that reuses prior agent output as prompt text
Require provenance tags on all datastore entries
Review one representative flow for prompt-injection handling
requires-engineering: add input sanitization and instruction/data partitioning

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs, uploaded files, and model provider/tool credentials, while Rasa handles text and voice over allowlisted network egress. If the pair shares a workspace or datastore, sensitive chat content can flow into Flowise and then out through configured model providers or HTTP tools. The shared-workspace path is not explicit, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are deployed against the same workspace or datastore
IF Flowise flows send uploaded or stored content to external model providers or HTTP tools
mitigations: Restrict Flowise to a separate workspace
Remove sensitive fields from Rasa transcripts before handoff
Audit outbound tools in Flowise for data exfiltration
Rotate any exposed model-provider keys
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise has write_filesystem and broad network egress; Rasa has allowlisted egress and no multiple-instance support. If both operate on the same mutable resources, they can overwrite each other's artifacts or race on shared conversation state. The profiles do not show locking or isolated directories, so the conflict is plausible in default deployments but not proven high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or datastore
IF shared mutable conversation state is updated without locks
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Turn on per-agent locking around shared state
Check for concurrent writes during one test run
Limit Rasa to read-only access where possible
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based orchestrator that can emit tool outputs, and Rasa is a customer-support bot that can act on dialogue. If Rasa consumes Flowise output as authoritative without verification, a mistaken or malicious Flowise response can cascade into incorrect support actions. The profiles suggest the pathway but do not document a direct action chain, so medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF Rasa uses Flowise-generated text as a decision input
IF no verification or human review step exists before downstream action
mitigations: Insert a verification step before acting on Flowise output
Require confidence thresholds for automated actions
Log and sample-check one day of handoffs
Disable auto-action on low-confidence responses
requires-engineering: add structured output validation

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only explicitly touch chatflow inputs/outputs or text/voice, with no stated regulated-data residency mismatch. The main compliance concern is logging/retention overlap on conversational data, but the profiles do not show a concrete breach path. Because the evidence is sparse and no special residency issue is documented, this stays low.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is routed through both agents
IF their logging or retention settings differ on the same data class
mitigations: Confirm retention settings for both systems
Redact personal data before storage
Review one sample transcript for compliance fields
Document data-flow ownership
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies
